I am 54 years old and have been farming in Quzhou for 25 years. My household has two people—my wife works off-farm, so I manage the 72 mu myself, though I rent in 64 mu of it. Cotton is my main crop and my livelihood; I plant 70 mu in early April with hybrid seeds at about 1 jin per mu. I rotary till and use plastic film mulch. For fertilizer, I spread 80 jin of general 15-15-15 compound fertilizer as basal dressing—that works out to about 6 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium per mu. I have a well and use border irrigation, but I only irrigate the cotton once during the season because too much water hurts the bolls. The biggest job is spraying: I need 13 insecticide sprays for bollworms and 2 herbicide sprays, so 15 pesticide rounds in total, plus 3 plant growth regulator applications to control height. On the side, I plant 2 mu of sunflower in mid-February and harvest it in early July. It is less work and brings in extra cash. I give it 100 jin of the same compound fertilizer and irrigate it 3 times, with 2 bug sprays and 1 weed spray. Last year I got 800 jin per mu from cotton and 550 jin per mu from sunflower, so I expect about the same this year if the weather holds.
